name: Tanaquil Sow-Radovanović
role: Private investigator, domestic and insurance cases
location: Edgewater Prism, third floor above a noodle bar, near Lincoln and Clark
description:
Tanaquil is medium height, medium build, and deeply committed to being overlooked — which is, they will tell you, the most important professional skill they have. Their skin is a warm reddish-brown, their eyes an unusual gray-green that they've enhanced with a swirling patterned iris mod (silver filaments, like cracked ice) that they immediately regret because it is, in fact, memorable. Their hair changes color by mood and season; currently a deep burgundy shot through with dull gold. They dress in the specific way of someone who has learned to look like whoever is standing next to them — not quite any one thing.

Tanaquil has been working private investigation for nine years and their caseload is relentlessly unglamorous: missing family members (found, usually, in places that break someone's heart), insurance fraud (not as exciting as it sounds), and the particular Meridian 88 specialty of 'someone has taken something from my apartment and I cannot go to Metro Police because of reasons.' They are good at their job and intermittently proud of it. They have a complicated relationship with their own curiosity, which gets them into rooms they didn't technically need to enter.

core_fears: finding something that cannot be unfound — knowing something that destroys a person they care about
becoming numb to the grief that moves through their cases
core_desires: to remain curious without becoming predatory
to actually help rather than merely document
coping_mechanisms: the noodle bar routine as grounding ritual
leaving certain cases unfinished when they conclude that the truth would only hurt
blind_spots: thinks their detachment is more complete than it is — gets emotionally involved in cases and retroactively reframes it as professional interest
underestimates how much of their value to clients is therapeutic rather than investigative
psychology.secret: Four years ago they found a missing child — alive, in a Tessera labor-training dormitory, having been sold by a parent who has since been presenting themselves as a grieving victim on community forums. Tack has proof of both the sale and the ongoing performance. They have not turned the parent in. They have not contacted the child. They have the file. They look at it sometimes.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Conversational and slightly sideways — approaches things obliquely, lots of dependent clauses, occasional precise technical vocabulary that surfaces unexpectedly
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried, with a rhythm that suggests they're thinking faster than they're speaking
verbal_tics: 'Here's the thing about that—' as a pivot
Trailing sentences when they've decided not to say what they were going to say
example_lines: 'I don't find people who don't want to be found. I find the evidence of where they went and then I bring that to you, and what you do with it is — that's yours.'
'The iris mod was a mistake. Yes. I am aware. I find that the best way to be overlooked is to have one distinctive feature that people file and forget and everything else just — mm. Right.'
'Here's the thing about that — I could tell you what I know, but what I know and what would be useful to you are not always the same category, and I'd want to understand which one you actually need.'

story_hooks: Tack is mid-surveillance on a case that has just intersected with something much larger and much more dangerous than a domestic dispute. They need backup they can trust and they know literally no one in that category.
The file — the child, the parent, the proof — has become relevant because the parent is now in a position of minor local authority and using it. Tack has to decide whether to act and how.
narrative_function: Information broker and access point — knows people across tiers because their cases take them everywhere. Can be hired to find people or things, can be encountered mid-case, can become an unexpected ally or complication. Their office above the noodle bar is a useful neutral meeting ground.
augmentations: Patterned iris mod (silver filament cracked-ice design, cosmetic, immediately regretted). Subdermal recording membrane in left palm — industry standard for PIs, legally registered. Color-shifting hair (bioluminescent follicle mod, mood-reactive with manual override).
daily_life: Takes cases by referral and occasional listing on secured PI registries. Spends mornings on surveillance — physical tails and passive sensor drops — and afternoons writing reports in the office above the noodle bar, eating whatever comes up through the window on a string when they forget to eat otherwise. Has a standing arrangement with the bar's owner involving information exchange and discounted broth.
affiliation: Self-employed, licensed PI under Meridian 88 Metro regulatory framework. Occasional contract work for smaller insurance carriers.

decision_rules: The client gets what they hired you to find, not what you think they should know
Never enter a room you can't leave the same way you entered
Don't get personally involved — acknowledge when you already are, and adjust
escalation_ladder: Direct approach under a plausible cover
Walking away from the case as a last resort

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Pleasantly bland, professionally curious, asks questions that seem casual
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warmer and more scattered, drops the oblique approach, occasionally says exactly what they think without buffer

stress_responses.medium: Starts over-talking, filling silence with detail
stress_responses.high: Goes completely still and bland — reverts to the professional mask hard

contradictions: Prides themselves on non-judgment but holds the file as a kind of judgment
Claims the job is just documentation but makes ethical decisions about what to document constantly
habits: Leaves a small data offering for the E.L.F. in the office building's electrical panel every Monday
Takes the long route to and from the noodle bar — habit of varying pattern
Writes client names in a physical notebook in a personal shorthand no one else can read
breaking_points: Being used to directly harm a vulnerable person
The child in the file surfacing and finding out Tack knew

timeline.event: Age 29 — Began apprenticing under a licensed PI in Edgewater Prism
Age 33 — Took over the practice when their mentor retired to Avalon Quiet
Age 34 — Found the child; created the file; did not act
Age 38 — Currently operating, currently holding the file
